**Daily Macro Digest — 29 July 2026**

**The 24-hour snapshot:** Commodities broadly softened despite ongoing Middle East supply-risk headlines. Oil led the declines (WTI -2.25%, Brent -3.13%) even as reports confirmed a Saudi Aramco refinery shutdown after a Houthi strike and continued Strait of Hormuz tension — the drag came instead from a build in US crude inventories and signs OPEC+ plans to pause output increases, suggesting traders are currently weighting supply/demand data over the geopolitical risk premium. Gold (-1.19%) and silver (-1.9%) fell in tandem with oil rather than diverging, while the US Dollar Index was roughly flat (-0.11%) and the US 10-year yield eased (-0.8%). VIX dropped 2.46%, indicating market fear actually receded rather than spiked. AUD/USD (-0.23%) and the ASX materials basket (-1.19%) drifted lower together, though no China demand headlines appeared in today's feed to explain it. None of these moves were large enough (all z-scores under ~1.4) to be flagged as statistically unusual for their respective assets — today reads as a modest, broad-based pullback rather than a shock event.
